result.title: Alignment via Generalization
result.summary: AI systems can become better at achieving the goals we give them without becoming better at doing what we actually want. Studying this alignment problem rigorously requires a framework connecting measurable performance to intended behavior. We propose Aligned-PAC learning, whose central idea is to reduce alignment to generalization: does success on the requirements used for training extend to requirements the system has not encountered? Rather than express our entire intention through a single training objective, we represent its different aspects through a collection of specific requirements. This perspective already yields strong theoretical results. We show how independent evaluation can provide rigorous evidence of alignment across the represented requirements, and establish how much evaluation is needed. We also develop an optimization method that, under explicit assumptions, combines learned models to satisfy the training requirements. The framework does not solve alignment in full: choosing requirements that faithfully capture our intentions, and understanding when learning will generalize to unseen requirements, remain open challenges. It provides a foundation for making these questions precise and studying them with the tools of learning theory.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Aligned-PAC 学习框架，把对齐问题转化为泛化问题：将意图拆解为一组具体要求，研究训练所覆盖的要求上的成功能否推广到未见过要求，并给出独立评估需要多少证据的理论结果及组合模型的优化方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关联，但其「训练要求→未见要求的泛化」及评估充分性分析，可能为 LVR 中推理监督是否迁移到新任务要求、需要多少验证证据提供概念参照，可供核查。
